must_remember: Nuclear fusion involves light nuclei combining to form heavier nuclei, yielding a positive mass defect and releasing energy according to $E = \Delta m c^2$.
The primary energy source in the Sun is the proton-proton (p-p) chain, releasing approximately $26.7\text{ MeV}$ per complete cycle.
Deuterium-Tritium (D-T) fusion has the lowest ignition temperature and highest cross-section, making it optimal for terrestrial controlled fusion.
Quantum tunneling is essential for fusion because classical thermal energies ($\sim 1\text{ keV}$) are vastly lower than the Coulomb potential barrier ($\sim 100\text{ keV}$ to $\text{MeV}$).
The Lawson criterion specifies the threshold condition of plasma density ($n$), confinement time ($\tau_E$), and temperature ($T$) required for ignition.

glossary.meaning: The difference between the total rest mass of individual nucleons and the rest mass of the bound nucleus.
The electrostatic repulsive potential barrier between two positively charged nuclei that must be overcome for them to interact via the strong nuclear force.
The quantum mechanical phenomenon where a particle penetrates a potential energy barrier higher than its kinetic energy.
A figure of merit used in nuclear fusion research that defines the minimum $n \tau_E T$ product required for a self-sustaining fusion reaction.
The narrow energy window in a thermal plasma where the product of the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution and the quantum tunneling probability is maximized.
